newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA TRY TO BLOCK RONALDO MOVE TO INTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA TRY TO BLOCK RONALDO MOVE TO INTER.

text.p: Barcelona have made a last-ditch effort to stop striker Ronaldo moving to Italy's Inter Milan by invoking a FIFA rule that would prevent his unnegotiated transfer to a non-Spanish club.
"For Ronaldo to go to Inter they have to negotiate with us," a Barcelona official told Reuters on Friday.
But Inter president Massimo Moratti said that would be impossible. "There is no dialogue because Barcelona does not want to sell Ronaldo," he said in Milan.
Inter had looked likely to pay the 4.5 billion pesetas ($30.1 million) stipulated in Ronaldo's contract as the price needed to release him from his obligations with Barcelona.
It is normal practice in Spain for players to sign contracts including such clauses, known as 'withdrawal clauses'.
But FIFA recognise such contracts only for transfers made within Spain.
"With them (Inter) the withdrawal clause is invalid," said the Barcelona official "In that case Ronaldo is untransferable."
As a result, Barcelona claim, Ronaldo could move only to a Spanish club unless the transfer were negotiated.
Speculation has already begun that Barcelona's arch-rivals Real Madrid could buy the Brazilian international before selling him on to Inter.
Real president Lorenzo Sanz has even raised the prospect of Ronaldo joining the Madrid club itself.
"We'd like to have Ronaldo. It's an interesting subject," said Sanz.
Barcelona vice-president Joan Gaspart hit straight back.
"If a Spanish club...acted as a 'bridge', then it would be fraud which could be easily proved," said Gaspart.
Ronaldo, who is currently with the Brazilian national squad in France, has said he will not play again for Barcelona.
"I will not play the Cup final (on June 28), not because of the fans but because of the management," said Ronaldo.
Moratti, who said on Thursday that he had an agreement with the player, declared himself surprised by the latest twist.
"We are surprised," he said. "I have put the matter in the hands of able lawyers in Italy and Spain. I hope to understand the situation better," he told reporters.
"We never announced anything. We merely said we had an agreement with the player, without anything being signed. If there are obstacles at the end of the month it won't be formalised.
"However if we can do this deal, we will do it. If it can't be done then it won't be."
